_doc: THE DISPATCH-SHAPE KEYSTONE (PLAN §17.1 — the highest-leverage piece). The dispatch analogue of role-registry.json: role-registry owns role IDENTITY (name·home·tier·kind·provider·model·build_chain·claude_pinned); THIS file owns the dispatch SHAPE policy — for each role/skill, the allowed dispatch shapes, the allowed tool ID, the cwd/file-scope/env/secret policy, timeout, budget, output policy, required fixtures+reviewers, and coverage obligations. Every dispatcher (dispatch-claude.js · dispatch-agent.js · future dispatch-skill.js / dispatch-api.js), the N-1 coverage gate, and the drift scanners READ FROM HERE so 'best dispatch shape per unit' is enforceable infrastructure, not doctrine. A role's CLASS is DERIVED from its role-registry attributes via `class_derivation` (single source of identity — no duplicated role list), then merged: defaults <- class <- role_overrides. The three operator-named dispatch failures map directly to contract violations: (i) skipped-gauntlet => a binding_verdict reviewer with no completion record (coverage gate); (ii) API-when-CLI => the `api` shape used by a role whose allowed_shapes lacks it; (iii) in-process-when-subprocess => the `in-process-agent` shape used by a role that forbids it (build-chain). Reader+validator: scripts/dispatch/dispatch-contract.js. Enforcer: scripts/dispatch/dispatch-contract.test.js (planted-violation P5) + scan:dispatch-contract (report-only first, then blocking per PLAN §4).

related.plan: runtime/agent-system-plan/PLAN.md (§17.1 keystone, §North-Star menu, §2 failures, §17.4 coverage record)

shapes._doc: The dispatch-shape menu (PLAN §North-Star). context_cost = the load on Alpha's context. `forbidden_for` names structural prohibitions the validator enforces.

inline.right_when: light work, OR work that needs the LIVE conversation (e.g. session:end handoff)

in-process-agent.right_when: small Claude returns that genuinely need orchestrator context (manager/lead/director consults, β); claude-pinned visual review (MCP/Playwright)
in-process-agent._note: BLOCKED for build-chain (dispatch-guide §2.5) AND for cross-provider reviewers (running a Claude clone silently kills provider diversity — the §2(iii) failure).

subprocess-claude.right_when: build-chain Claude roles; heavy Claude skills (§13)

subprocess-cross-provider.right_when: independent review/security (model diversity; the no-verdict-on-own-work invariant)

api.right_when: ONLY a provider capability with NO CLI (deep-research, GPT-Pro/API-only models)
api._note: PLAN §3/N-2: API availability NEVER implies API dispatch. CLI is mandatory for agent dispatch.

defaults._doc: Applied to every role unless its class or override changes them.

class_derivation._doc: Ordered rules over role-registry attributes. The reader takes the FIRST match. `when` keys are ANDed; a missing key is a wildcard. This keeps the role list single-sourced in role-registry.json — adding a role there auto-classifies it here.

face._doc: alpha/beta/gamma/delta/epsilon — one identity, run as the harness session.

build_chain_worker._doc: frontend/backend/security builders+fixers, stub-scaffold — edit a repo, MUST be isolated.

cross_provider_reviewer._doc: frontend/backend reviewers, qa-reviewer (openai), security-reviewer (antigravity/agy — the Gemini lab; the individual gemini CLI is sunset) — independent verdict on a different model family. The security panel's Claude HUNTER lane is the sanctioned in-process-agent exception (sanctioned_lanes.security_claude_hunter; ADR-0016).

claude_pinned_reviewer._doc: design-quality, visual-review, test-runner — judgment is VISUAL (Playwright-MCP), so Claude-pinned; independence is the BINDING VERDICT, not provider diversity (a sanctioned carve-out).

cross_provider_consult_lead._doc: cross-provider lead/director — the GPT product-leadership chain (design-lead, product-lead, director-of-product, director-of-growth): routes via subprocess-cross-provider like a reviewer; advises and authors but does not emit a binding verdict. The class encodes dispatch SHAPE, not org seniority (seniority lives in role-registry `tier`) — a GPT director and a GPT lead share this identical shape, so they REUSE this class rather than minting a director variant (β DECIDE 2026-06-17, E-DISPATCH-PERFECT-001 W2; the contract's anti-exception principle). Provider diversity preserved for the lead/director's authoring work. Mirrors cross_provider_reviewer shape with binding_verdict:false.

manager._doc: directors + leads (incl. quality-lead) — small Claude returns that need orchestrator context; dispatched via the Agent tool, recorded via record-inprocess.

tool_cross_provider._doc: learner — cross-cycle meta-review on a different family (sees the Claude builder/reviewer shared blind spots).

role_overrides._doc: Per-role exceptions merged LAST (defaults <- class <- override). Empty by design — exceptions are a smell; prefer fixing the class derivation. Documented carve-outs only.

epsilon._note: ε is the sprint conductor: runs inline as the session; its own shape is inline. The in-process roster (`in-process-agent`: managers/leads/design-quality/visual-review) is summonable directly by the ε CONDUCTOR in ANY spawn context — top-level (α wearing the ε face) OR a teammate-spawned ε — via the harness Agent tool, each spawn supplying a `scopeContract` (the scope-contract-guard is the real gate). ED-041 ('Agent unavailable inside subagents') is RETIRED as a per-spec misstatement: a Claude subagent HAS the Agent tool iff its spec lists it, and ε's does (ADR-0014; re-verified 2026-06-18 + live-confirmed by the E-TEAMS-MIGRATION-001 teammate-ε). The spawn-hand stays with the conductor — a summoned roster member must NOT dispatch the build chain or cascade further, guaranteed STRUCTURALLY by scripts/checks/consult-roster-no-dispatch.js (a NON-EXEMPT consult role's spec carries no Bash/Agent (the one exemption, quality-lead, retains Agent — ED-065), so it can't dispatch by construction; the dispatch-route-guard in-process build-chain block is a narrow backstop). A node SCRIPT still cannot call Agent (the ε runtime returns `requires-orchestrator` to hand that spawn to the ε-agent); ε also drives the CLI-routable roster (subprocess-claude builders via dispatch-claude.js, subprocess-cross-provider reviewers via dispatch-agent.js).

mode_profiles._doc: PLAN §8.7 / S-LC-06 — per-mode dispatch permission profiles. A mode profile NARROWS which dispatch shapes a role-CLASS (`class_shapes`) or a specific role (`role_shapes`) may use WHILE IN THAT MODE. β SECURITY INVARIANT (load-bearing): the class_derivation + role-registry constraint is the HARD CEILING — a mode profile can ONLY REMOVE a shape, NEVER ADD one the class/role does not already allow. A role gated to `subprocess-claude` MUST NOT resolve to `subprocess-cross-provider` just because a mode 'grants' it. Every shape a profile lists for a class/role MUST be a SUBSET of that class/role's own `allowed_shapes`; `dispatch-contract.js validate` FAILS a profile that widens past the class (the planted-widen test asserts this). Omitting a class/role = the class default applies (no narrowing). REPORT-ONLY ramp this sprint — additive; no dispatch is blocked on a mode profile yet (the runtime narrowing in validateDispatch is defense-in-depth, gated on an explicit `mode`).

adhoc._doc: α+β+γ. Build-chain is Gamma-only; teammates β/γ only (team-guard). Builders → subprocess-claude; reviewers → cross-provider; managers/leads/visual → in-process. Each is the class default (identity narrowing — a valid subset).

sprint._doc: ε conducts the full lifecycle; REAL dispatch on both route classes (CLI builders + cross-provider reviewers) + the in-process roster (managers/leads/visual-review).
sprint._alpha_only_note: ADR-0014: NO shape is α-only. The `in-process-agent` shape (managers/leads/design-quality/visual-review) is summonable by the ε CONDUCTOR in ANY spawn context — top-level (α wearing the ε face) OR a teammate-spawned ε — via the harness Agent tool, each spawn supplying a `scopeContract`. The prior α-only overlay (added in 975ed5c) encoded ED-041 as a doctrine; ED-041 is RETIRED as a per-spec misstatement (a Claude subagent has the Agent tool iff its spec lists it; ε's does — re-verified 2026-06-18 + live-confirmed by the E-TEAMS-MIGRATION-001 teammate-ε). The array is kept (empty) rather than removed so a reversal is a one-line re-add (ADR-0014 reversal plan). The real gate on a roster spawn is the scope-contract-guard (scopeContract required, fail-closed); the spawn-hand stays with the conductor — a summoned roster consult MUST NOT dispatch the build chain or cascade (guaranteed STRUCTURALLY by scripts/checks/consult-roster-no-dispatch.js — a NON-EXEMPT consult role's spec carries no Bash/Agent (the one exemption, quality-lead, retains Agent — ED-065); the dispatch-route-guard in-process build-chain block is a narrow backstop; ε remains the sole builder-dispatcher). CARVE-OUT: a non-Claude orchestrator (Codex) has NO harness Agent tool at all — not because of ED-041, but because it is not a Claude-harness agent — so it uses CLI routes only. This annotation does NOT narrow class_shapes.

oneshot._doc: δ standalone skeleton build. Build-chain via subprocess-claude (isolated worktree); no cross-provider reviewers required for a skeleton run.

solo._doc: Alpha builds directly, agents-when-helpful — flexible but still INSIDE every class ceiling. No extra narrowing beyond the class defaults.

sanctioned_lanes._doc: SP-20260611-001 fix 2 (T-311 / crossfam finding A.2): a sanctioned lane is a NAMED, NARROWLY-SCOPED dispatch that is INTENTIONALLY off the class default shape — registered HERE (registry-as-SoT) rather than suppressed by a wrapper-local `!blocking` conditional. The dispatch-contract reader's `sanctionedLane({role, shape, lane})` returns sanctioned:true ONLY when ALL of: (a) the lane name is registered here, (b) the role's DERIVED class is in the lane's applies_to_classes, AND (c) the proposed shape equals the lane's shape. A sanctioned lane is ADDITIVE and REGISTER-ONLY: it changes NO validateDispatch exit path and grants NO new shape to validateDispatch — it is a separate consult the wrapper makes so the informational note prints in BOTH report-only and blocking (ENFORCE) modes and the sanctioned lane NEVER exits 1. A genuinely-mismatched NON-sanctioned shape under blocking still refuses exactly as before. NO wildcard (redteam: sanctioned-lane over-breadth) — each lane enumerates its exact classes + the one shape it sanctions.

review_fallback._doc: The --review-fallback lane (dispatch-claude.js): a cross-provider REVIEW role is routed through subprocess-claude (a Claude clone) INTENTIONALLY when its normal provider (openai/gemini) is quota-dead. Honest visible debt — the completion record still stamps fallback:true + provider:claude + quota_fallback_from so coverage-gate sees the cross-provider debt; this lane only stops the W2 ENFORCE flip from BRICKING the fallback exactly when it is most needed. READ-ONLY review roles only — build-chain roles are refused this lane upstream (dispatch-claude.js guard, T-305 G2).

security_claude_hunter._doc: ADR-0016: the security 3-lab panel's Claude HUNTER lane (security-reviewer.third_pass, claude-opus-4-8@max) + its fable-5 planner/judge are the ONE legal Claude shape for a cross_provider_reviewer — in-process-agent, summoned by ε via the harness Agent tool with a scopeContract, evidenced by a record-inprocess completion (the same ok:true record gauntlet-verify reads). NOT a fallback (that is review_fallback) — a DELIBERATE cross-lab hunter. A node script cannot summon it (requires-orchestrator); dispatch-review.js fires the agy + gpt CLI passes and hands the Claude lane to ε. Registered here so the informational note prints and the lane never exits 1; the class default still forbids in-process-agent for every non-sanctioned reviewer dispatch.

skills._doc: SEEDED for skill-execution-routing (PLAN §13) — NOT yet earned. A skill is `inline` until it PASSES §13.6 (runs headless) AND §13.7 (pays + good). `subprocess` entries below are CANDIDATES (classified by weight) carrying subprocess_verified:false until a real smoke run stamps them. The reader treats an unverified `subprocess` skill as `inline` (fail-closed: never trust an unverified subprocess classification). REPORT-ONLY this release.

session:end._note: learn/mine/sleep/TRACKER-reconcile are subprocess-able; the handoff needs the LIVE conversation -> inline-required. Split, don't route wholesale (§13.5).
